title: Roll back the document processor alias to its known-good version
eligibility_checks: A recorded known-good version exists with a verified passing canary.
The current alias version is not already the known-good version.
Fresh evidence shows a configuration mismatch on an allowlisted field (RESULTS_TABLE or SCHEMA_VERSION).
The processor execution role fingerprint matches the trusted deployment manifest for both versions.
contraindications: AccessDenied evidence alone, with no corroborating deployment/config diff, is insufficient -- request more evidence instead.
No known-good version is recorded, or its canary never passed.
The alias already points at the known-good version.
Weighted/linear routing is active on the alias.
The execution role differs between the current and known-good versions -- this is an IAM change, out of scope for this runbook.
verification_checks: Synthetic canary invocation returns no function error.
The canary result record exists in the expected results table with the expected payload hash.
The invocation ExecutedVersion matches the approved target version.
Post-update alias configuration matches the approved version and remains unweighted.
steps: Confirm the incident has a recorded known-good version with a passed canary (deployment_manifest.is_known_good and canary_passed).
Confirm the currently deployed alias version differs from the known-good version and is not itself the known-good version.
Confirm the alias uses unweighted routing (no canary/linear traffic shifting in progress).
Confirm the failing version differs from known-good on an allowlisted field (RESULTS_TABLE or SCHEMA_VERSION) via get_release_diff.
Confirm the processor execution role is unchanged between versions (processor_role_matches_manifest is true) -- this runbook only covers configuration rollback, not IAM changes.
If all checks pass, the eligible action is: point the alias back at the known-good version, preconditioned on the alias revision id observed during investigation.
After the alias update is applied, invoke a synthetic canary request and confirm its result record exists with the expected payload hash.
Re-read the alias configuration after the canary and confirm it still points at the approved version with unweighted routing.
Only after both checks pass may affected customer requests be considered eligible for replay; replay is a separate bounded, explicitly-approved step.
